title: PRAHARI-SIM conference storyboard (SPEC §11) — edit captions and bookmarks here; no rebuild needed

steps.title: The forest and the satellite pixel
steps.caption: A Terai-style forest with nodes 70 m apart. One VIIRS pixel (375 m) covers about 29 of our node cells.

steps.title: Fixed thresholds
steps.caption: Cheap sensors with fixed thresholds: alarms all day long — and there is no fire.

steps.title: Haze on a wet morning
steps.caption: Haze lifts every node at once. PRAHARI holds what is common to the whole network (SCMR).

steps.title: The same haze with SCMR off
steps.caption: Switch that mechanism off, and here is what you get. (S toggles SCMR, R toggles RAQ.)

steps.title: A fire on a dry, busy afternoon
steps.caption: A fire starts by the path. Smoke drifts downwind; two nodes raise candidates, then the edge confirms.

steps.title: Every alarm explains itself
steps.caption: Why this alarm: the SCMR ratio, Fisher's combined p-value, the prior, and the posterior against the threshold.

steps.title: The satellite race
steps.caption: PRAHARI confirmed this fire hours before the satellite alert — no overpass could see it until the evening.

steps.title: Results
steps.caption: Over the full protocol: far fewer false alarms than fixed thresholds — and removing any mechanism makes it worse.

steps.title: Everything here is simulated
steps.caption: Every model, equation, assumption and source tag is listed. All numbers are simulation output (SIM).
